small_guidance:
- Transpose W to K-major (W_t of shape [K, N], contiguous) once in __init__ so the inner B-load is contiguous along N; currently w_ptrs uses stride_wn (=K) on the N axis which is strided. This should materially improve B-load bandwidth at BLOCK_N=128/256.
- Add larger-tile autotune configs now that M=N=K=8192 (e.g. BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=4; and BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, num_stages=4). Drop the smaller 64-wide tiles — they will never win at this size.
- Since K=8192 is divisible by 64, force EVEN_K=True path and consider BLOCK_K=128 with num_stages=3 to deepen K-pipelining on the 4090.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a split-K or stream-K GEMM: with M=N=8192 there are only 64×64=4096 output tiles at 128×128, which already saturates the 128 SMs, but stream-K can balance tail tiles and squeeze ~10–15%. Alternatively, persistent-kernel scheduling with one program per SM looping over tiles eliminates launch overhead and improves L2 reuse.
- Store weights pre-transposed (K-major) as a buffer so both A and B loads are contiguous on the K reduction axis; fuse the (bias - sub) * mul precompute into a small init-time buffer (already done) and keep the ReLU+affine epilogue on the accumulator.
- Consider fp16/bf16 accumulation path via tl.dot with TF32 already on; explore casting inputs to bf16 on-the-fly inside the kernel to double tensor-core throughput, then accumulate in fp32 — only valid if the 5e-2 tolerance permits (it does).
